title: Blue Roof Assessments following Hurricane Michael
description: Blue Roof Assessor Tyler Crubaugh from USACE Little Rock District, discusses Blue Roof Assessments while working in Panama City, Fla., following Hurricane Michael. (Video by Chris Gardner)
keywords: Michael, armyhurricaneresponse, hurricanemichael18, armyhurricanemichael, USACE, Hurricane
unit_name: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers South Atlantic Division

transcript.text: - My name is Tyler Crubaugh from
Ozark Powerhouse, Little Rock.
My reason I'm here is for
the Hurricane Michael relief effort.
The Blue Roof Program basically allows people
to be able to stay in their residence
and keep the water out.
It basically is a temporary roof.
I am assessing the amount of roof,
the style of roof, any other deficiencies in the roof
to make note for the contractors.
The majority of what you're needing to get
when you're doing the assessment
is your measurements from the ground
and projecting your pitch of your roof
to be able to give you your multiplier,
to be able to give you your mathematical formula
for your blue roof square footage.
The reason we've come to Florida with an overall mission
with the corps for the blue roof team
is to help them get on the path towards recovery.
